cards.question: Should leftovers from one dinner count as lunch the next day?

blocks.paragraph: The spec fills seven dinners and seven lunches, but it never says whether last night's dinner can be tomorrow's lunch. This one is yours to call, because it depends on whether households want to plan around leftovers or cook fresh every time.

bullets: If leftovers count, plans need fewer recipes and shopping lists get shorter.
If they do not, every meal is a new recipe, so plans stay varied but take more cooking.
Either way the spec needs one clear sentence about it before the build starts.

context.title: The line that leaves it open

blocks.quote: Each day has one breakfast, one lunch and one dinner slot, and every slot is filled with a different recipe.

options.label: Let leftovers fill a lunch slot
options.consequence: Plans need fewer recipes and shopping lists get shorter, but the same recipe can show up twice in a day.

options.label: Require a different recipe for every slot
options.consequence: Every meal is a new recipe, so plans stay varied but need more cooking and a longer shopping list.

recommendation.text: Let leftovers fill a lunch slot.
recommendation.reason: Most weekly planners are used to save effort, and leftover lunches are the common way to do that.

cards.question: Is the shopping list rounding rule what you meant?

blocks.paragraph: When the planner builds the shopping list, it rounds each ingredient up to the next whole package. The rule decides whether the list leans toward buying too much or too little, and that is a product choice.

blocks.quote: Quantities on the shopping list are rounded up to the nearest purchasable package.

recommendation.reason: Rounding up avoids a second trip to the store, and the spec already says amounts are shown before rounding.

cards.question: Do you want past weekly plans kept after the week ends?

blocks.paragraph: The spec covers making and editing the current week's plan. It says nothing about what happens to that plan once the week is over.

bullets: Keeping old plans means more storage.
It also means a new screen to browse them.
That makes it a call about scope, so it is yours.

cards.question: Which day should a weekly plan start on?

blocks.paragraph: A plan covers seven days in a row, but the spec does not name the first day. That day decides where one plan ends and the next begins, and households disagree about it.

blocks.quote: A weekly plan covers seven consecutive days.

options.label: Start the week on Monday
options.consequence: Plans line up with the working week, but a household that shops on a Sunday plans across two weeks.

options.label: Start the week on Sunday
options.consequence: A Sunday shop covers the week ahead, but plans no longer line up with the working week.

recommendation.reason: Most calendars and work schedules begin on Monday, so plans match how people already think about the week.

cards.question: Should a plan remember a household's dietary needs?

blocks.paragraph: Today a person can pick any recipe for any slot. The spec says nothing about allergies or diets. Remembering them would add a settings screen and a filter on every recipe list, so this is a scope call.
